page.title: Flows
page.purpose: Author, validate, and browse reusable device flows, including the capability gap report that says whether a given device can run one.

priorities.statement: A flow's capability requirements and the resulting gap report are shown before any run can start.
priorities.notes: A pre-execution gap is actionable; a mid-run failure is wasted device time and confusing evidence.

priorities.statement: Each step shows which resolution rung it will use on the selected device.
priorities.notes: The difference between a deterministic and an inferred step is what a reviewer most needs to see.

priorities.statement: Bounded wait policies are shown with their upper bounds.
priorities.notes: A named bound is reviewable; a raw sleep is not.

states.description: A saved flow opened against a device that satisfies every step.
Flow definition and capability check in flight.
No flows authored yet; explains how to create one or promote an agent run.
The flow is valid and the selected device satisfies some but not all steps — the gap report is the page's primary content.
The capability snapshot behind the gap report predates the probe interval; the report is labelled as computed from an old probe.
The flow or capability request failed; the page says so rather than presenting an empty gap report as a clean bill.
Flow under edit; validation runs continuously.
Validation errors shown per step, blocking run.
Flow is valid but the selected device cannot satisfy some required capability; the gap is enumerated with its cause and whether it is fixable.
Valid and fully satisfied by the selected device.

elements.name: Device
elements.description: Which device the flow is being checked against. The gap report is meaningless without it.

elements.name: Gaps
elements.description: The enumerated capabilities that block steps, each with its cause and whether another strategy would satisfy it.
Runnable and blocked step counts plus the overall verdict.

elements.name: Plan
elements.description: The flow's steps in order, each annotated with the rung or capability it will use on the selected device.
Per-step resolution rung — semantic, visual-anchor, vision — or the capability that blocks it.
The named bounded policy and its upper bound for each wait step.

elements.name: Run flow
elements.description: Dispatch. Unavailable while a known gap exists, because dispatching despite one is the only error state here.
Run only the steps the selected device satisfies, as an explicit partial choice rather than a silent skip.
Re-evaluate the same flow against a different device or strategy.
Per-step authoring errors, distinct from capability gaps.
Empty-state guidance covering both authoring a flow and promoting a successful agent run.

claims.statement: The capability gap report is perceivable before the flow can be dispatched.
claims.rationale: Priority 1 and OT-P0-005. A mid-run capability failure wastes device time and produces evidence nobody can interpret.

claims.statement: A gap report is presented as a successful, structured answer rather than as a failure state.
claims.rationale: D-010 makes the gap report a successful response; the visual treatment has to match, or the most common honest answer this scenario gives will read as breakage. Manual because it is a tone judgement rather than a presence check.

claims.statement: A capability gap is perceivably different from an authoring validation error.
claims.rationale: One means the flow is wrong; the other means the device is not equipped. Conflating them sends the operator to fix the wrong thing.

claims.statement: The unqualified run control is not offered while a known gap exists.
claims.rationale: D-010: dispatching despite a known gap is the only error in this flow, so the UI should not make it the default affordance.

claims.statement: Running only the satisfied subset is offered as an explicit, separately labelled choice.
claims.rationale: Silently skipping blocked steps would produce evidence that looks complete. Making the partial run a deliberate act keeps the resulting record honest.

claims.statement: Every step shows the resolution rung it will use on the selected device, or the capability that blocks it.
claims.rationale: Priority 2 and D-004. The deterministic-versus-inferred distinction is what a reviewer most needs, and it is cheapest to show before the run.

claims.statement: Each wait step shows its named policy and upper bound.
claims.rationale: Priority 3 and OT-P0-005. An unlabelled wait is indistinguishable from a sleep, and an exceeded bound must be an evidence-visible failure rather than a longer wait.

claims.statement: The device the flow is being checked against reads before the gap verdict it produced.
claims.rationale: A verdict without its subject is unreadable — the same flow is runnable on one device and blocked on another.

claims.statement: The empty state explains both authoring a flow and promoting a successful agent run.
claims.rationale: Promotion is the compounding path in OT-P1-006, and it is not discoverable from a blank list.
